summary: Kickoff for Crestview Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered onboarding timeline, infra requirements, security checklist, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, initial benchmarks, and next steps. Customer is aiming for pilot in mid-Jan with security review complete before production. Action items assigned for onboarding materials, benchmark runs, and compliance docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the CSM on this account. We've got Carlos our SE and Devon from implementations with us. Quick round of intros?
[00:20] Lena (Crestview): Hi all, Lena here, Head of AI at Crestview. Marcus, Aisha and Ravi are on the call too.
[00:32] Carlos (Redwood SE): Hey, Carlos here, I'll be your technical lead for the setup, focusing on perf and network.
[00:40] Marcus (Crestview): Marcus, platform eng. We'll own infra changes, I'll be coordinating VPN and allowlist.
[00:50] Aisha (Crestview Security): Aisha, security. I'll be the main compliance contact.
[00:58] Maya: Great. The agenda is quick: confirm goals, review infra checklist, decide hosted vs dedicated for pilot, run initial benchmarks, and align on timeline. Any additions?
[01:15] Lena: Sounds right. Our top goals are: low latency for clinician-facing features, patient data residency, and strict auditability. Pilot target mid-Jan.
[01:28] Maya: Perfect. Quick question on data: will the data flow be PII into Redwood hosted endpoints or do you anticipate on-prem?
[01:38] Marcus: For pilot, we want private deployment inside our VPC if possible. Some PHI will be involved, we need KMS/HSM support and audit logs.
[01:52] Aisha: Also, SOC 2 scope—what parts of the infra are in scope if we use Redwood hosted? Need to confirm encryption at rest and key control.
[02:10] Carlos: Totally. Redwood supports Private deployments with customer-managed KMS, we also have Dedicated capacity if you want predictable throughput without full private control. I might say Redwood Dedicaed (sic) — apologies — dedicated capacity gives reserved GPUs and SLA.
[02:28] Ravi (Crestview): Can you clarify the difference between Private and Dedicated for us? Network-wise and security-wise?
[02:40] Devon (Redwood): Sure. Private (VPC) deploy means our control plane still manages the service but it's isolated to your VPC and you manage keys; on-prem is fully customer-run. Dedicated is hosted — Redwood manages infra but reserves a pool just for you, so less network config but more limited in terms of key control.
[03:05] Lena: So Dedicated = less ops on our side but not full key control, Private = more work but meets policy. Is that right?
[03:14] Carlos: That's right. Also performance differences: dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower multitenant variance, private can be tuned but depends on your infra.
[03:30] Marcus: For pilot we prefer Private or Private-like; security team prefers customer-managed keys. We can do a hybrid if needed.
[03:43] Maya: Noted. Next, timeline — pilot mid-Jan means we need onboarding docs and initial infra access this week. We'll send the onboarding checklist today.
[03:55] Carlos: I'll also propose a minimal benchmark matrix: 1) 512-token generation latency p95, 2) concurrent 4 rps throughput, 3) prefix KV cache impact. We can compare hosted small model vs dedicated quantized model.
[04:12] Lena: Great. Do you have recommended model family for clinician-facing prompts? We need high accuracy and low hallucination.
[04:21] Carlos: We typically recommend Llama-3-style open models with Redwood-verified tuning, and sometimes we apply post-processing checks. We'll share model profiles.
[04:35] Aisha: On compliance, requirement: audit logs retained for at least 2 years, SSO via SAML, and encryption with customer KMS. Can Redwood provide proofs?
[04:48] Maya: Yes — we have SOC 2 docs, SAML SSO support, and KMS integrations. I'll share the security pack. The SOC 2 attestation includes hosted and dedicated, private deployments have a different control set.
[05:05] Marcus: IP allowlist — we need a list of IP ranges to allow. Also whether port 443 only or other ports.
[05:13] Carlos: We'll provide exact egress/ingress ranges for both hosted and dedicated. For private VPC peering we may need specific steps. 443 is standard for API.
[05:30] Ravi: Any special network config for KV cache or stateful components?
[05:36] Carlos: No special ports, it's TCP over HTTPS; the KV cache is internal to runtime. Sometimes in our notes it's called KV cash in transcriptions, haha.
[05:48] Lena: On success criteria: acceptable p95 latency under 350ms for 256 token responses, and cost per call under X (we'll fill in). Pilot acceptance depends on security signoff and two-week reliability.
[06:05] Maya: We'll capture those as SLA targets and put them in the pilot acceptance doc.
[06:12] Devon: Implementation steps: 1) Access & creds, 2) Network config, 3) Baseline tests, 4) Short integration, 5) Security review, 6) Pilot. We can do 1-3 before year end.
[06:28] Marcus: For creds, we'd prefer a short-lived token flow and RBAC so engineers have limited scopes.
[06:36] Carlos: Redwood supports token-based and SSO flows; we also have route-level RBAC.
[06:44] Aisha: Also need data residency confirmation — logs and model cache behavior. If we run private in our region that's easiest.
[06:54] Maya: We'll note region requirements; we do support EU/US regions.
[07:02] Lena: Can you send any sample evals or prompt sets to measure hallucination?
[07:08] Carlos: Yes. We'll share sample eval prompts and a simple quality script. We'll also include instructions to run the eval harness.
[07:20] Maya: Question about billing and Dedicated commit — does the pilot need a commit?
[07:26] Devon: Not for pilot. Dedicated is typically reserved with a commit. For pilot you can use hosted credits or temporary dedicated trial if you want to test throughput.
[07:40] Marcus: If we test dedicated performance, what is the lead time for a dedicated pool?
[07:45] Carlos: Usually 2-3 weeks for allocated GPUs depending on region. For quick comparisons we can emulate with burst configs.
[07:56] Lena: Ok. Security question — will Redwood accept a vendor security questionnaire?
[08:02] Maya: Yes, send it to security@redwood.ai and Aisha we'll loop in our security engineer, Sofia.
[08:12] Aisha: Great. Also need any third-party subprocessors list.
[08:18] Maya: We'll include subprocessors in the security pack.
[08:25] Marcus: For the bench matrix, do you have a script we can run in our infra to compare?
[08:30] Carlos: Yes, we have a lightweight benchmark harness and a spreadsheet template; we'll upload both.
[08:38] Lena: Any gotchas for VPC peering? We have strict routing and can't accept inbound from unknown sources.
[08:45] Devon: We'll provide a step-by-step; sometimes customers set up a proxy or NAT for outbound only. We'll work with your network team.
[08:56] Lena: Sounds good. Next, ramp plan and contact points — who owns what?
[09:02] Maya: I'll own onboarding coordination and weekly check-ins. Carlos will handle tech and benchmarks. Devon handles implementation schedule. Marcus — infra; Aisha — security.
[09:15] Marcus: Noted. On docs we need explicit runbook for failover and fallback to a less-capable model if latency spikes.
[09:24] Carlos: We support routing policies and fallback to smaller models. We'll document recommended fallback policies.
[09:34] Ravi: About KV cache — is the cache persisted across requests or per-session?
[09:40] Carlos: It's a runtime KV cache that persists for active sessions; you can persist prefixes depending on config. We'll clarify in the runbook.
[09:52] Lena: Timeline recap?
[09:55] Maya: Action items: I'll send onboarding deck + security pack by Dec 22. Carlos will run baseline bench and share by Dec 29. Marcus to provide network details by Dec 24. Aisha to share SOC 2 scope and any vendor questionnaires by Dec 22. Deep technical dive with infra team in Jan week 2.
[10:20] Aisha: That timeline works.
[10:24] Maya: Any other questions or concerns?
[10:28] Marcus: Not right now. We'll review the docs when you send them.
[10:32] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[10:35] Maya: Great — thanks all. We'll follow up with the materials and schedule.
[10:40] Carlos: Thanks, bye.
[10:42] End of recording.
